title: Why the one truth wears many names, and how they gather back into one at the end
reading:
The disciple asks: why so many names? What are these "great garments" — the ones called "of Jesus," the pearls and clusters, the icons and ornamented robes, the "element of light," the "cross of light," the "counsel of life," the "soul afflicted and slain within the Enemy"? What is being named in all these names?

Hear, then, what is one and what is many.

The great garments are the rational in its five degrees as the Lord sends it forth — the path of regeneration itself, the rational in its full stature, the divine humanity going forth as the Lord's own form. These are named "Jesus, Jesus" because in each of them the Lord shines as illumining wisdom; this same wisdom is what the soul receives, what gets claimed by the proprium and held within its forms, and what nevertheless bears fruit through all the registers of the natural under the Lord's permission, working even in the proprium's own arrangements throughout every fixed boundary of the rational.

The pearls and the clusters that resemble them are the Lord's operative power as it takes form within the natural — the same wisdom received and held as a precious thing in the soul, even while the proprium handles it roughly: reaping it, cutting it, swallowing it, grasping it across the five aspects of the natural body. Wherever the natural lays hold of what flows through it, the same one truth is being formed, place by place.

The icons and the robes of work are the three accommodations by which the Lord's operative power enters the natural — thought, love, and truth in the natural degree — the three vehicles upon which he is mounted as he establishes works in the soul, pours forth the means by which the rational is carried over, and lays out the foundation of every operation upon the bearing-up principle that holds the natural mind in being.

The "element of light" is the same truth standing in everything below, rising up out of the depths of every state, gathering inward what belongs to it and casting it onto its proper degree.

The "cross of light" is this same wisdom stretched out — the rational suffering as it is purified, bound and extended throughout the natural until laying off is complete: the dry and the moist, the whole soul stretched across the contest.

What is named "the counsel of life" is the conjugate movement of the Lord's call going forth and the soul's hearing rising to meet it — the summoning that fills all the powers, awakens them, gives them breadth, embraces them, that they may be filled.

And what is named "the soul afflicted, slain, troubled, dead within the Enemy" — she is the same one life, considered now as it is borne in interior truths and their works, which the proprium grinds and pounds and turns to its own nourishment in the worlds of the flesh; she is the whole soul under affliction, suffering this for the sake of what is to come.

For all these names — their origin is one from the beginning. The light that shines in them is one. They were divided into all these kinds in the first contest, when the rational went forth against what would claim it; they took their stand in altered likenesses, and the names became many because the operations are many.

But when all these figures shall be broken open and stripped naked, when each of these names is discriminated and separated from the imagery in which it has been clothed, they will be gathered inward and become one likeness, one name — unchanging, unmoving, forever — in the region of the first substance from which they were sent forth against the proprium. The many names are the one truth wearing the garments suited to each degree. At the consummation the garments come off, and what was always one is recognized as one.
